title: Directory-connector member import (ldap_import) skips org-policy enforcement (check_user_allowed), bypassing the Single-Organization and required-2FA policies
summary:
## Summary
The directory-connector / bulk member-import endpoint `POST /api/public/organization/import`
(`src/api/core/public.rs`, `ldap_import`) activates and re-activates organization members **without
calling `OrgPolicy::check_user_allowed`** - the policy gate that every interactive
membership-activation path applies. A member admitted or re-admitted through directory sync is
therefore never checked against the organization's **Single-Organization** or **required-2FA**
policies. This is the one activation path missed by the fix for #1849.

## Relationship to prior art (a precise incomplete-fix residual, not a rediscovery)
- **#1849** ("org two-step-login policy enforcement doesn't work", CLOSED) is the fix this residual
  belongs to: it added `OrgPolicy::check_user_allowed` to the interactive membership-activation
  paths. **This report is the one activation path that fix missed** - the directory-connector import.
- A separate report of mine is the **sibling instance of
  the same pattern** - "a check present on the primary path, absent on an alternate path." The two
  together motivate a systemic audit of alternate entrypoints (see last section).
- **#6780** ("SSO user bypasses org 2FA", OPEN) is an acknowledged **same-class** bypass on a
  **different** path, confirming the maintainer treats this enforcement area as live.
- A refresh-token / security-stamp advisory is **distinct** - a membership revoke does not rotate the
  security stamp, so it does not cover this scenario (confirmed empirically on 1.36.0).

## Affected versions
- `1.36.0` and earlier - confirmed on 1.36.0.
- Fixed in `1.37.0`: `ldap_import` now calls `OrgPolicy::check_user_allowed` after `restore()` and re-revokes members the policy disallows.
- The `check_user_allowed` enforcement (added for #1849) covers the interactive activation paths but
  was never added to the public-import path.

## Root cause
Issue #1849 was fixed by adding `OrgPolicy::check_user_allowed` to the membership-activation paths -
`_confirm_invite` (`organizations.rs:1427`), `restore_member_impl` (`organizations.rs:2402`),
`accept_org_invite`, `edit_member`, and the admin path. `check_user_allowed`
(`src/db/models/org_policy.rs:283`) enforces **both** the Single-Organization policy and the
required-2FA policy.

The directory-connector import endpoint `POST /api/public/organization/import`
(`src/api/core/public.rs`, `ldap_import`) was missed: it re-Confirms a revoked member via
`member.restore()` (~`public.rs:87`) **without calling `check_user_allowed`**. (New members are
created as `Accepted` (~`public.rs:107-110`) and would still be checked at the admin `confirm` step;
the airtight bypass is the `restore()` → `Confirmed` path, which skips `confirm` entirely.)

## Impact

### Primary - Single-Organization policy bypass (needs no 2FA at all)
A member who should be blocked/removed by the Single-Org policy is silently re-Confirmed via directory-connector
import, because the import path skips the `check_user_allowed` enforcement every interactive path
applies. Clean policy bypass, no 2FA involved.

### Demonstrated - required-2FA policy bypass (ring-6 chain)
The same missing check lets the import re-Confirm a member with **no 2FA** into a **required-2FA**
org. The member then retains org-data access via the refresh-token grant (`identity.rs:refresh_login`),
which - unlike `password_login`/`sso_login` - does not run `enforce_2fa_policy` (the revoke
mechanism). The member is never re-revoked, so the owner's mandatory-2FA policy is defeated for them.

Reproduced on a fresh self-hosted instance (vaultwarden 1.36.0 / main `d6a3d53`):

| Step | Action | Member status / access |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Member M Confirmed, no 2FA, has collection access | `Confirmed`; sync returns 1 org cipher |
| 2 | M password-login (policy off) | refresh token captured |
| 3 | Owner enables required-2FA policy | -> Revoked (enforcement works at enable-ti...
